subject: Computer Networking
title: 5G: Speed, Latency, and Capacity
description: A 60-second lesson on 5G: Speed, Latency, and Capacity.

hook.text: 5G isn't just faster 4G. It's three networks in one: high speed, massive connectivity, and ultra-low latency.

buildup.text: Enhanced mobile broadband delivers gigabit speeds. Massive IoT connects millions of sensors per square kilometer.

discovery.text: Ultra-reliable low latency targets 1 ms delay. That enables remote surgery and autonomous vehicle communication.

twist.text: Millimeter wave 5G is blazing fast but barely penetrates walls. Sub-6 GHz 5G has better range but lower peak speeds.

climax.text: Carriers blend both. Mmwave for stadiums and downtowns, sub-6 for broad coverage. It's a layered strategy.

punchline.text: 5G serves three very different needs with one standard.

quiz.question: What are the three service categories of 5G?
options: Enhanced broadband, massive IoT, and ultra-reliable low latency

details.summary: 5G delivers dramatically faster speeds, lower latency, and higher device capacity than 4G through three spectrum tiers. Low-band provides wide coverage, mid-band balances speed and range, and mmWave delivers multi-gigabit speeds over short distances.
details.whyItMatters: 5G is not just faster phones — it enables new categories of applications like autonomous vehicles, remote surgery, and massive IoT deployments that require its unique combination of speed, latency, and capacity.
takeaways: Three spectrum tiers trade off speed, range, and penetration
Sub-1ms latency enables real-time applications like remote control
Network slicing creates virtual dedicated networks per application

faq.question: What are the three 5G spectrum bands?
faq.answer: Low-band below 1 GHz provides wide coverage similar to 4G with modest speed improvements. Mid-band from 1 to 6 GHz offers the best balance of speed and coverage for most users.

faq.question: What is 5G network slicing?
faq.answer: Network slicing creates multiple virtual networks on the same physical infrastructure. A hospital could have a low-latency slice for remote surgery while a factory has a high-reliability slice for robotics. Each slice has guaranteed performance characteristics.
